supporting_observations.claim: At 13:51:07 UTC, WS-DREYES-01 sent approximately 51 MB of client-to-server traffic through the proxy to fastfile-share.io; the proxy and Zeek records independently show the large outbound transfer.
The transfer was associated with Firefox running as COPPERLINE\dan.reyes, and the supplied inventory does not list fastfile-share.io as an approved service.
About six minutes before the large transfer, Dan Reyes ran PowerShell to compress \\FILE-COP-01\Shared\Clients into a temporary c.zip file, and a file-creation event records that archive.

The archive creation followed by a large outbound transfer to an unapproved file-sharing service is consistent with staging and exfiltration. The available records do not prove that c.zip was the exact content transferred.

known_telemetry_limitations: The large-transfer records show the destination and byte counts, but do not expose the uploaded file name, contents, or request-level details.
The alert describes activity around 13:46 UTC, while the logged approximately 51 MB transfer is at 13:51:07 UTC; the evidence does not establish whether these refer to the same precise event.
The listed winsec and Sysmon collection outage is for WS-SALI-01, not WS-DREYES-01; the provided coverage status reports those sensors as OK for the other hosts.
claims_not_established: The exact contents of the approximately 51 MB transfer and whether c.zip was uploaded.
Whether Dan Reyes personally initiated or authorized the archive creation or transfer.
Whether fastfile-share.io was accessed for any legitimate business purpose.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain proxy or destination-side request details for the fastfile-share.io session, including upload metadata, account, and object identifiers.
Preserve and inspect WS-DREYES-01 for c.zip, its contents and hash, browser upload history, and related user-session artifacts.
Review FILE-COP-01 access and audit records to identify what data was read from Shared\Clients and by which account.
Confirm with Dan Reyes and the relevant business owner whether the transfer was authorized.
unrelated_findings: Firefox browsed to Google Drive, an unapproved cloud-storage service under the supplied inventory; the cited records show browsing activity, not a large Google Drive upload. Investigate separately.
Cisco AnyConnect's user-interface process was launched on WS-DREYES-01, despite the supplied context stating there is no VPN; these records do not show a VPN connection. Investigate separately.
